name: 08-moonlive-effects
description: Scripting the lights in the browser: a library effect downloaded and run, then one written from nothing, from a single line to a particle system.

steps.title: MoonLive effects
steps.description: Write the lights, in the browser
steps.caption: MoonLive effects. Writing the lights, in the browser.
The grid here is two fifty six by two fifty six: sixty five thousand lights, so there is room to draw something.
Everything that paints lives under a layer, and that is where this one is going.
Clearing what is there, so you see the effect arrive rather than replace something.
A MoonLive effect is a script the device compiles itself, into native code, on the chip.
Pick one from the library and the device fetches it, compiles it and runs it, while you watch.
Nebula: a noise field births the light, and a curl flow folds it into a cloud. Twenty lines of script.
That one ships with the device. The next one does not exist yet, so I am going to write it.
A fresh effect, with no script behind it at all.
The plus asks for a name and creates the file on the device. I am calling it m l e demo.
Typed into the editor, character by character. One line, corner to corner, and the lights follow the moment I save.
One call draws a circle, and the fourth argument is how thick the stroke is. Two of them, one inside the other.
Now a for loop per axis, and an if. Every band fills to its own beat, sixty five thousand times a frame.
A control the script declares appears on the card by itself, and changing it applies on the very next frame.
And the finish: the same power functions the built in effects use. A particle pool, gravity, drag and ageing.
Six hundred sparks, thrown, pulled back and aged, over sixty five thousand lights. All of it written in the browser.
